title: Para Shooter Rakesh Nidagundi, a Designer Who Found Shooting by Accident, Targets Asian Para Games Gold
excerpt: The 38-year-old from Hubballi took up shooting during lockdown, won a World Championship team silver in Changwon, and backs India's 13 shooters to win 13 medals in Aichi-Nagoya.
body:
• Para rifle shooter Rakesh Nidagundi, 38, from Hubballi, contests his first Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, in the 10m air rifle SH1 category.
  • Nidagundi found the sport by accident: a graphic designer, he was hired to design material for a shooting academy, tried the sport during the Covid lockdown, and was competing nationally by 2021.
  • He won a silver team medal at the WSPS World Championship in Changwon, his first international medal, and holds three national golds.
  • He predicts India's 13-strong para shooting squad, which includes Avani Lekhara and Manish Narwal, can win 13 medals.

Rakesh Nidagundi designs his own destiny these days, but shooting found him by accident. The 38-year-old from Hubballi, whose legs were affected by polio in childhood, was working as a graphic designer when a local shooting academy ordered design work from his office, the Times of India reported via NewsPoint. Coach Ravichandra Balehosur invited him to try the sport. During the Covid lockdown, with no design work, he did, and fell for it.

A Fast Rise

He started shooting in 2020 and competed at his first nationals, a Paralympic Committee of India event in Delhi, in 2021. He has since shot six national competitions and won gold at three of them, according to ANI via Latestly.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2111406006005809544

"I am from a middle-class family. I had to struggle financially. My coaches supported me," he said. He came through the Khelo India scheme to the National Centre of Excellence, and last year joined the Vijayi Bharat Foundation, which supports his coaching, equipment, training and nutrition, including new rifles and international coaches.

The Changwon Silver

His third international event brought his first international medal, a silver team medal at the WSPS World Championship in Changwon. "It was my third international competition. It was my first international medal. It was a very happy moment for me," he said.

Thirteen Shooters, Thirteen Medals?

Nidagundi now contests the 10m air rifle SH1 at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games, his first multi-sport event, with para shooting scheduled for October 19-20 and 22-23. India's 13-strong squad includes two-time Paralympic gold medallist Avani Lekhara and Paralympic gold medallist Manish Narwal. India won six para shooting medals at the last Asian Para Games, two of each colour, in an edition where the full contingent passed 100 medals for the first time.

"We have 13 athletes participating this time. All of them are elite athletes. I think we have a 100 per cent chance of winning 13 medals."

— Rakesh Nidagundi, para rifle shooter

On the support structure behind the rise, he is direct: "When I came in 2021, I struggled for 2-3 years. After that came Khelo India. Since then, para-sport is getting a lot of support."

The Squad Around Him

The 13-member para shooting contingent also includes Amir Ahmad Bhat, Mona Agarwal, Nihal Singh, Rubina Francis, Rudransh Khandelwal and Swaroop Mahavir Unhalkar, among others, in a smaller overall Indian contingent at Aichi-Nagoya that is still targeting a record medal haul. Para shooting is one of eleven sports on India's programme, running alongside para athletics, para badminton and para swimming through the Games.
